key_insight: Physis-Lang argues that language can serve as a physical representation for video world models if it is allowed to self-evolve with the model. Instead of relying only on extra visual or numerical signals, the framework uses language to capture and refine physical knowledge for more realistic prediction.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between visually plausible video generation and physically correct world modeling. Existing video world models often ignore or fail to encode basic physics, leading to impossible motions, interactions, or state changes.
method: Introduces a self-evolving language-based framework called Physis-Lang to represent physical knowledge.
Uses language as the main medium for encoding, updating, and refining physics-related concepts during model learning.
Aims to improve video world model predictions by aligning generated dynamics with physical principles rather than only visual realism.
impact: This work suggests a simpler and more interpretable path to physically grounded video generation and world modeling. For practitioners, it points to language as a scalable alternative to adding complex extra modalities for physics reasoning.

paper_title: Physis-Lang: Self-Evolving Language as a Physical Representation for Video World Model
paper_authors: Liming Lu, Xianzheng Ma, Wenkun He, Guanqi Zhan, Yilin Zhao
